hero.subtitle_html: Wangs → Pizolhütte → five glacial lakes circuit → Pizol (2844 m) — SAC T2 · ~900 m gain · ~12 km · ~5–6 h

intro_html:
"One of Switzerland's most celebrated alpine walks — five glacial lakes gleaming like jewels below the Pizol massif. Each lake has its own character, from the dark mirror of the Schwarzsee to the turquoise shimmer of the Pizolsee at 2400 m."
— Glarus Alps hiking lore

The Pizol 5-Seen-Wanderung links five glacial lakes in a single circular walk above Pizolhütte (2227 m): Schwarzsee (2157 m), Baschalvasee (2232 m), Schottensee (2244 m), Pizolsee (2400 m) and Wildsee (2390 m). The circuit is rated T2 — wide mountain paths, no exposure — making it accessible to fit beginners. The optional push to the Pizol summit (2844 m) upgrades the day to T3 with a further 617 m of gain and panoramic views from the Rhine valley to the Bernina.

Schottensee (2244 m) — midpoint of the circuit, cradled in a high alpine cirque with views back toward Bad Ragaz.

routes_subtitle: (lake circuit T2; Pizol summit optional T3)

routes.title_html: 1. 5-Seen-Wanderung circuit — cable car from Wangs (recommended, T2)
bullets_html: Take the Pizolbahnen cable car from Wangs (506 m) or Bad Ragaz up to Pizolhütte (2227 m).
Head south-west from Pizolhütte, dropping slightly to Schwarzsee (2157 m) — the darkest, most brooding of the five lakes.
Climb west past Baschalvasee (2232 m) and Schottensee (2244 m), both reached on wide, well-marked paths.
Continue north over the Wildseelugge saddle to Pizolsee (2400 m) and then south-east to Wildsee (2390 m).
Return to Pizolhütte for lunch, then descend by cable car. Circuit ~10–11 km, ~650 m gain, ~4–5 h.
The five-lake sequence is clearly waymarked with the yellow hiking-path blazes.
routes.source: SAC Route Portal, Pizolbahnen operator, and hikr.org

routes.title_html: 2. + Pizol summit extension (T3, adds ~2 h and 617 m gain)
bullets_html: From Wildsee, follow the signed ridge path north-east to Pizol (2844 m). The final 200 m gain involves short scrambling sections on good holds — T3.
Summit panorama covers the Rhine Valley, Liechtenstein, the Säntis massif, the Glarus Alps and (on clear days) the Bernina.
Descend south back to Wildsee or directly to Pizolhütte via the marked descent ridge. Total with cable car: ~12 km, ~900 m gain, ~5–6 h.
routes.source: SAC Route Portal, Pizolbahnen operator, and hikr.org

routes.title_html: 3. Full ascent on foot from Wangs — no cable car (T2/T3, ~9–10 h)
bullets_html: Start in Wangs (506 m) and ascend through Pardiel, Gaffia, and Laufböden to Pizolhütte — ~1720 m gain over ~7 km.
Join the lake circuit at Pizolhütte. Continue to Pizol summit (optional).
Descent back to Wangs via the same route or via Furt. Total: ~16 km, ~2340 m gain — a long, demanding day.
routes.source: SAC Route Portal, Pizolbahnen operator, and hikr.org

getting_there.by_car_html: Drive to Wangs (canton St. Gallen), signposted from the A13 motorway at junction Bad Ragaz. Paid parking at the Pizolbahnen base station. Alternatively park in Bad Ragaz — a gondola connects Bad Ragaz to Pardiel then Pizolhütte.
getting_there.by_pt_html:
• Train: Zürich HB → Sargans (≈50 min, IC/IR) or → Bad Ragaz (≈55 min).
  • From Sargans: Postbus 190 to Wangs, Pizolbahnen (≈10 min).
  • From Bad Ragaz: local bus or short taxi to Wangs cable-car base, or use the Bad Ragaz gondola.
  • Plan via sbb.ch. The Pizolbahnen timetable and summer operating hours are at pizol.com.

day_plans.footer_html: Check cable-car operating hours in advance at pizol.com. First gondola is typically 08:00–08:30 in summer; last descent by ~16:30–17:00.

lapse_rate.example_html: Example: valley forecast 15–25 °C → Pizol summit ≈ 0 °C to +10 °C. Lakes at 2200–2400 m will be ~8–9 °C cooler than the valley.

sources_html: MeteoSwiss — best Swiss forecast. Use the Bad Ragaz or Wangs point; select the mountain layer for summit conditions.

The ridge above 2600 m is fully exposed. Thunderstorms build fast in the St. Gallen Alps — descend or shelter in Pizolhütte if convective cloud develops.
weather.season_html: Summer hike only. Best window: late June to mid-October. The lakes may still be partially frozen and the paths icy in early June — check the Bergsommerbericht on pizol.com.

webcams.label: Pizol — summit webcam looking north toward Bad Ragaz and the Rhine Valley. Best direct view of summit conditions.
Wildhaus / Gamserrugg (Toggenburg) — ~30 km north-west; useful indicator of approaching north-side weather and visibility over the St. Gallen Alps.

takeaways_html: The cable car is the key logistical decision: Pizolbahnen runs from both Wangs and Bad Ragaz — the Bad Ragaz gondola has a longer ride and slightly more scenic approach, but Wangs is faster from Sargans by bus. Book or check operating hours in advance in shoulder season.

The five lakes are best done counter-clockwise (Schwarzsee → Baschalvasee → Schottensee → Pizolsee → Wildsee) so the steeper sections are ascents not descents, and you arrive at Wildsee with maximum energy for the optional Pizol summit push.

By late August the Pizolsee shrinks noticeably — earlier in summer (July) gives higher water levels and more dramatic reflections. The Schwarzsee is darkest in the morning when shadows pool in its cirque.

The summit of Pizol (T3) is a short but genuine scramble on good granite — poles should be stowed for the final section. Views extend to the Rheintal, Liechtenstein, Säntis, and on perfect days the Bernina massif to the south-east.

reports.title: Pizol 5-Seen-Wanderung: alle fünf Seen in einem Tag
bullets_html: Classic counter-clockwise circuit from Pizolhütte: Schwarzsee first, then the upper trio of lakes before Wildsee.
Trail well-marked throughout; even on busy summer weekends the circuit never feels crowded beyond the Pizolsee viewpoint.
The Schottensee section offers the most dramatic views of the Pizol ridge towering overhead.

reports.title: 5-Seen + Pizol Gipfel: T3-Erweiterung lohnt sich
bullets_html: After Wildsee, the Pizol summit path is signed and in good condition — short scramble at T3 on solid rock.
Summit view is among the best in the eastern Swiss Alps: Säntis, Churfirsten, Silvretta, and the long Rhine Valley below.
Allow an extra 2 h and start by 08:30 to be off the exposed summit before afternoon convection.

reports.title: Pizol von Wangs zu Fuß — ohne Seilbahn
bullets_html: Full ascent from Wangs via Pardiel, Gaffia, Laufböden: a genuine mountain day of ~2340 m gain.
The lower valley path through Wangs' farming hamlets is pleasant but long — factor in ~3 h before you even reach Pizolhütte.
Descent via Furt offers a different perspective; public bus back from Wangs in the evening.

gear.title: Mandatory
items_html: Sturdy hiking boots (B-grade, ankle support) — trail is rocky at the lakes
2–3 L water + electrolytes (no reliable water source between lakes)
Sun protection: hat, sunglasses, SPF 30+ (high UV above 2200 m)
Layers: base + insulating + windproof / rainproof shell (lake saddles can be cold and windy)
Hat + gloves if going to the Pizol summit
Phone with offline SwissTopo map + GPX
Cash / card for Pizolhütte café and cable car

gear.title: Recommended
items_html: Trekking poles (helpful on descent from Pizol summit)
Camera — the five lakes each reward wide-angle shots
Binoculars — ibex are common on the Pizol ridge in summer

gear.title: Pizol summit only
items_html: Helmet not required but T3 scramble means poles should be stowed
Gloves for wind on the ridge
Extra 30 min buffer in your schedule

safety_html: Lightning: the ridge above Pizolhütte is fully exposed. Check MeteoSwiss before departure and descend to the hütte if convective cloud builds.
Early-season ice: the Wildseelugge saddle and paths near Pizolsee can be icy in early summer — microspikes recommended before mid-July.
Crowds: the 5-Seen-Wanderung is one of Switzerland's most popular hikes. Weekday starts avoid the worst congestion near the lakes.
T3 summit scramble: the Pizol summit section requires sure-footedness on good rock. Not recommended in wet conditions or for children without alpine experience.
Cable car schedule: missing the last gondola means a 1700 m descent on foot — always note the last departure time.
Phone reception: good at Pizolhütte and on the ridge; patchy in some lake cirques. Download maps offline.
Emergency: Rega 1414 · European emergency 112. Pizolhütte has a phone.
This is a summer route only. Winter and early-spring conditions involve avalanche terrain on the upper slopes.

disclaimer_html: Compiled from the SAC Route Portal, German Wikipedia, Pizolbahnen, and hikr.org references. Not professional mountain-safety advice. Conditions in the Alps change rapidly — glacial retreat has altered some paths near the lakes in recent years. Always re-check MeteoSwiss, the SAC situation warnings, cable-car operating status, and any trail closures before setting out.
